scope: Proposition 3.7 (Vanishing reach) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a > 0. Under the band law, explore all components meeting Fn \ Dn. The probability that any visited vertex is in a fixed neighborhood of supp g tends to zero in (3.1). The same conclusion holds for an exploration starting from a fixed positive-area region on one side of a separating positive-width band and reaching a fixed closed region on its other side, provided the closure of the starting region and the target have fixed positive clearance from the band. The two gaps admit the mass-free covering families used below, with all clearances fixed before the lattice and band limits.
